name: Binary Search Pattern
description: Binary search repeatedly halves the search space by comparing the middle element against the target. It only works on sorted (or monotonic) sequences, but the 'predicate binary search' variant applies it to any monotonic boolean function.
how_to_identify: Sorted input, or a question that can be reframed as 'is a candidate answer valid?' with a monotonic true/false sequence.
use_cases: Finding first/last occurrence of a value
Finding the smallest divisor given a threshold
template: while lo < hi: mid = lo + (hi - lo) // 2; if predicate(mid): hi = mid (or lo = mid + 1); else adjust the other bound. Pick lo vs hi loop carefully to avoid infinite loops.
common_mistakes: Off-by-one errors causing infinite loops or skipped elements.
Applying it to unsorted data without sorting first.
related_problems: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
